title: Empowering Free Knowledge: Highlights from WikiCamp Morocco 2026 in Marrakech
content:
The Wikimedia Morocco User Group held its fourth annual event, “WikiCamp Morocco 2026,” in Marrakech from October 19 to 21, 2026. The theme was “From Contribution to Initiative; Let us Build Our Organizational Team Together.” Active members met to improve their skills in creating free online content, documenting languages, leading groups, and organizing local projects.

Building on past events, this year focused on hands-on practice, better time management, and clear results. The goal was to help members move from working alone to leading organized, lasting projects across Morocco.

The program covered many topics. Attendees reviewed past activities and checked on programs like “Wikipedia in the Classroom” and “Ambassadors of Free Knowledge.” They also looked at Moroccan Darija and Amazigh Wikipedia projects, held contests, learned about technical tools, and discussed new ideas needing volunteer help.

To help preserve local speech, a hands-on workshop focused on Moroccan Darija Wikipedia. Participants recorded local words, meanings, example sentences, and audio clips to save rare regional vocabulary for future generations.

title: Books for Bassam, on the occasion of the 12th anniversary of Wikimedia Côte d’Ivoire’s affiliation
content:
Every year, since its 10 years of affiliation with the Wikimedia Foundation, Wikimedia Ivory Coast celebrates its anniversary by giving. In 2024, for the first edition of this initiative, the association supports a center for social integration. In 2025, an orphanage. In 2026, for the third year in a row, Wikimedia Côte d’Ivoire is collecting books, educational games and materials for an Ivorian library that has suffered damage. And your support makes a difference!

Bassam, the choice for Wikimedia Côte d’Ivoire’s 2026 community service. The seaside town of Bassam (Grand-Bassam) is home to a Wikimedia Côte d’Ivoire club, known as WikiClub Grand-Bassam.

In June 2026, heavy rains flooded the library at the Raffaelo Masto Cultural Center, located within the Carrefour Jeunesse in Grand-Bassam. Established by the Communauté Abel, the library was open to everyone — from students to parents. It also offered young people and adults a range of activities and a pathway toward social and professional integration, providing educational support and promoting African literature.

title: Bringing Climate Education to All: Empowering Students with Disabilities Through Open Knowledge
content:
On June 20, 2025, a dedicated team from the Eco Warriors Movement, in collaboration with the Environmental Science Students’ Association at Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), visited the Ashanti School for the Deaf in Ghana. Our goal was simple yet profound: to conduct inclusive climate awareness training for students with hearing and visual impairments while supporting the school community with essential supplies.

This initiative is a core milestone of the project “Expanding Open Climate Education to Schools for Persons with Disabilities.” Supported by Creative Commons and executed in alignment with broader open knowledge principles alongside partners like Open Foundation West Africa and the Wikimedia Foundation, the project demonstrates how open educational resources (OER) and offline open technology can drive knowledge equity for underrepresented groups.

During the outreach, we engaged over 180 junior high and upper primary students, alongside seven staff members, including the Assistant Headmaster, Mr. Richard. Together, we explored urgent global and local environmental challenges, including:

  • Excessive energy consumption and energy efficiency

title: Afroyanga Bootcamp 3.0: Exploring Creativity, Culture, and Connection
content:
What does it take to bring a film from an idea to the screen?

During Day 3 of Afroyanga Bootcamp 3.0, delegates visited Trino Studios for an introduction to the creative and technical processes behind filmmaking.

The visit offered participants a glimpse into the different stages of film production: pre-production, production, and post-production.

During the discussion, delegates learned about the planning involved before filming begins, including casting, budgeting, and identifying suitable locations. They also explored what happens during production and the work that follows filming, such as editing, sound production, and colour grading.

One participant was particularly struck by how much work happens after filming has ended. A movie may take months or even a year to become ready for release, depending on the project and its production requirements.

The visit also revealed that the final version of a film may differ from the original script. Scenes can change, and producers and directors may need to work through different creative decisions as a project develops.
snippet: What does it take to bring a film from an idea to the screen?
creator: Linason Blessing

title: Wali Wikimedians Community Celebrates 14th Wikidata Birthday with a Step Towards Making Wikidata Accessible in Waali
content:
To mark the 14th birthday of Wikidata, the Wali Wikimedians Community organised a virtual birthday celebration and training session to introduce its members to translating Wikidata properties into the Waali language.

For the Wali Wikimedians Community, this special occasion was about more than cutting a birthday cake. It was an opportunity to make a meaningful contribution to the growth of Waali on the Wikimedia platforms and ensure that the language is represented in the global digital knowledge space for present and future generations.

The event took place on Friday, 30 October 2026, via Zoom. It brought community members together to celebrate Wikidata’s milestone while learning how to edit and translate Wikidata properties into Waali.

title: Wiki Loves Food India 2026: Celebrate India’s culinary heritage, one photograph at a time!
content:
From 1st to 30th November 2026, the Punjabi Wikimedians User Group is inviting all of India to take part in Wiki Loves Food 2026. It’s a national photography competition to celebrate the incredible diversity of Indian food, the traditional food culture and the richness of our culinary heritage.

Following the successful Indian editions of 2021 and 2022, Wiki Loves Food is back in 2026 with another chance for photographers, foodies and Wikimedia contributors to document and share the flavours of India with the world.

The competition is part of the international Wiki Loves Food 2026 photography campaign which is designed to showcase the food of different countries through freely licensed photographs on Wikimedia Commons.

Wiki Loves Food is keen to see photographs that illustrate the full breadth of India’s culinary heritage.

  • Meals and dishes: regional thalis, traditional home cooked meals, festive food, ceremonial food and community meals.
  • Street food and snacks: Chaat, local snacks, the roadside food stalls, the breakfast specialities and of course the tea.
  • Sweets and desserts: Indian mithai, Bengali sandesh, the various types of traditional sweets, festive desserts and the like.

title: Experiencing Language Diversity Conference 2026 as a Madurese Woman: Personal Reflection and More
content:
The Language Diversity Conference 2026 made me reflect on myself as a woman in the Wikimedia movement and on my journey over the past six years.

For all these years, the Madurese language has grown to have three Wikimedia projects. What makes me especially proud is that women have played a significant role in bringing these projects to life, especially Madurese Wiktionary and Madurese Wikisource.

Along the way, we have organized various activities to keep our community active and connected, including training sessions, monthly meetings, and informal gatherings at cafés. Although our café meetups do not happen every month, we hold them quite regularly as a way to connect, exchange ideas, and strengthen our relationships as contributors. Beyond our local activities, the Madurese community has also participated in various initiatives organized by Wikimedia Indonesia and the wider global Wikimedia movement. Through these opportunities, we can connect with other communities, share our experiences, and bring our language and culture into broader national and international spaces.

title: From Skills to Action: Expanding How We Contribute to Wikimedia
content:
Across the African Wikimedia movement, participation takes many forms. It can mean speaking confidently about Wikimedia to a potential contributor, improving the quality and visibility of an image on Wikimedia Commons, connecting Wikipedia articles to Wikidata, documenting the pronunciation of an African language, sharing community work through a Diff blog post, or making a first contribution from a smartphone.

From June to September 2026, the African Wikipedian Alliance created spaces for its members within the Anglophone and Francophone communities to build these practical skills, exchange experiences, and explore new ways of contributing through six learning sessions with 136 attendees recorded. Participants engaged with communication and advocacy, Wikimedia Commons, Wikidata, African language preservation, storytelling, and Wikipedia mobile editing.

Together, the sessions reflected a broader idea: building a stronger Wikimedia movement is as much about onboarding more editors, as it is about equipping those contributors with the skills, confidence, and opportunities to create, improve, preserve, connect, and share free knowledge.

title: Afroyanga Bootcamp 3.0: Empowering Youths Through Open Knowledge, Leadership.
content:
The Afroyanga Bootcamp 3.0, which was organised by African & Proud, which is led by the two Co founders Richard Edozie and Kolawole Oyewole the Bootcamp  unfolded through interactive learning sessions, practical Wikimedia training, conversations about volunteering and leadership, team games, and visits to creative spaces in Lagos, Nigeria.

The bootcamp brought together young people passionate about knowledge sharing, community development, and creating meaningful change across Africa. For participants, it was an opportunity not only to learn new skills but also to connect with fellow Wikimedians, reflect on their contributions, and discover how their interests and experiences could help make African knowledge more visible and accessible.

From understanding Wikipedia’s editorial policies to exploring Nigerian filmmaking and contemporary art, Afroyanga Bootcamp 3.0 demonstrated that promoting open knowledge goes beyond editing articles. It also involves understanding the people, cultures, institutions, and creative industries whose stories deserve to be documented.

title: Enthusiasm Was Never the Problem: The Case of Western Armenian Wikipedia
content:
At the Wikimedia CEE Meeting in Cluj-Napoca in September, I opened my talk by asking the room a question. Who here has heard of Western Armenian? A fair number of hands went up. Who knew about it two years ago? Fewer. Five years ago? Fewer still. Ten years ago? The hands came down slowly, one by one, until there were almost none left.

Then I introduced myself properly. Western Armenian is one of the two standard forms of modern Armenian. It is the diaspora one, spoken across Lebanon, Syria, Turkey, Greece, France, Argentina, Canada, the United States and so many more. No country administers it. It is not an official language anywhere; it has no ministry and no national broadcaster, and it received its own ISO language code, hyw, only in 2018. Its Wikipedia launched in 2019. Before that, our articles lived inside Armenian Wikipedia with a tag banner. Our user group has around forty-five regular editors spread across a dozen cities, and we have never had a physical office.

That took about ninety seconds, and I had not yet made a single point.

title: When Wikimedian partake in civic discussion: reflections from ICF 2025
content:
One of the ultimate goals of the Wikimedia movement is to preserve and share knowledge freely, without reservation or intimidation. To further this mission, representatives from the movement are frequently invited to take part in wider advocacy gatherings. The International Civic Forum (ICF) is one such prominent platform that I had the opportunity to attend last November (2025).

Hosted by the International Civil Society Centre—a Berlin-based organisation that supports civil society sectors worldwide—the ICF is an annual global gathering where civil society leaders discuss pressing challenges, explore strategic approaches, and seek opportunities for collaboration.

The 2025 edition took place in the heart of Bangkok, Thailand, at Thammasat University’s Tha Prachan campus—a historic site central to the country’s 1973 uprising and 1976 massacre. Held alongside International Civil Society Week (the world’s largest civil society gathering, co-hosted by CIVICUS and the Asia Democracy Network), the forum focused on the theme: “Advancing Rights Together: Shaping Strategies in the Face of Aligned Opposition”.

title: Queering Wiki 2026: Wikimedia LGBT+ holds first in-person conference in Montréal
content:
From October 23–25, a hundred LGBT+ knowledge enthusiasts from over 30 different countries gathered in Montréal, Québec, Canada, for Queering Wiki 2026. Organized by Wikimedia LGBT+ and Wikimedia Canada, funded by the Wikimedia Foundation, and sponsored by Wikimedia CH and Wikimedia Deutschland, this conference marked the first in-person global gathering of LGBT+ Wikimedians and allies, following virtual Queering Wiki events held annually from 2022–2025.

The QW2026 program kicked off with a Culture Crawl, offering a guided bus tour with information about the host city’s rich LGBT+ history. Attendees then participated in three days of sessions, including keynotes, lightning talks, posters, and presentations in three tracks: Knowledge Without Borders, Queer Histories, and Queer Futures. Sessions were offered in English, Spanish, and French, with live translation and transcription available via a smartphone app.

A keynote from Constance Crompton, the director of the Humanities Data Lab at the University of Ottawa, introduced the Lesbian and Gay Liberation in Canada (LGLC) project and its intersection with Wikipedia and Wikidata in making archival information available online.

title: Albanian Translation of the EduWiki Hub Starter Kit now available.
content:
The EduWiki Hub’s Newcomer’s Starter Kit, a comprehensive guide for integrating Wikimedia projects into education, is now available in Albanian. This translation was made possible by Vjollca Merdani, an educator, project manager, and active contributor to the Albanian Wikimedia community for over five years. With her extensive background in running educational programs and leading open knowledge initiatives, her translation brings this vital resource directly to Albanian speakers worldwide.

  • Clear, sequential instructions to help new volunteers and teachers bring Wikipedia into their lessons.
  • Action-oriented tools that help organizers build educational programs, run workshops, establish goals, and follow community guidelines.
  • Ideas, practical samples, and ready made exercises for coordinators working to create friendly, safe, and supportive environments for new members.
  • Community focused development created by participants to strengthen free learning through Wikimedia projects.
